title: A second governed workflow, its read guard, and the governed-only subtree
note: R55 said three things in prose that nothing checked: that only ONE workflow of the safest available kind used the substrate, that the ungoverned adapters remained the equally-good route to any byte in the workspace, and that verification re-derived digests without ever re-running the tool. G1-G3 attack the second tool's launchability -- the subprocess module was a literal in three places, so a default entry point would run the artifact writer under a record naming a different tool. G4-G7 attack the READ guard, which is the guard a write allowlist cannot supply: a tool that hashes paths a caller names can be pointed at results_gate_table.csv, and a governed digest of a canonical output reads as the substrate having mediated it. G8-G11 attack the governed-only subtree, including the two ways a re-entrant scope goes wrong. G12-G17 attack re-execution: the scratch directory, the verifier minting its own grant instead of borrowing the worker's, and the comparison itself. G16 and G17 SURVIVED the first run of this matrix and were treated as findings: nothing made the re-run disagree, so only the passing branch was exercised, and nothing asked what the comparison did when it covered no artifacts at all -- it answered with the same sentence it uses for a real one, and the guard that refuses that did not exist until G17 said so. G13 is the one that was found in production rather than by review -- the scratch path came from an attribute only the test fixture set, so the check ran for tests and raised AttributeError for the Snakemake rule.

mutations.name: G1_an_unmapped_tool_defaults_to_the_artifact_writer
mutations.rationale: a tool nobody mapped launches the artifact writer, so a typo in a registry entry produces a governed, capability-checked, evidence-backed record of the wrong tool having run

mutations.name: G2_every_tool_runs_the_same_entry_point
mutations.rationale: two registry rows point at one module: the registry reports two tools and the system runs one, which is the state the row described as ONE workflow of the safest available kind

mutations.name: G3_the_second_tool_is_not_registered_at_all
mutations.rationale: the registry entry no longer names the tool the workflow asks for, so the second workflow cannot run and default-deny reports it as an unregistered tool

mutations.name: G4_the_read_guard_is_removed
mutations.rationale: a governed run hashes any path the caller names, so results_gate_table.csv and /etc/passwd both land in a provenance chain as things a governed run read

mutations.name: G5_the_read_guard_reports_the_failure_as_success
mutations.rationale: a refused path is skipped instead of failing the run, so the index reports success over a subset nobody asked for -- the vacuous shape this repository has shipped once

mutations.name: G6_a_missing_file_is_skipped_rather_than_failing_the_run
mutations.rationale: an index over files that are not there completes, and the count in the report is the count of what happened to exist

mutations.name: G7_an_empty_file_list_produces_an_empty_index
mutations.find: if not isinstance(files, list) or not files:
mutations.rationale: zero files hashed reports exactly like a complete index; a verifier that reports success over zero items is worse than no verifier

mutations.name: G9_the_governed_prefix_set_is_empty
mutations.rationale: the guard is present, runs on every write and covers nothing -- a check that cannot fail, which is the defect the write allowlist replaced a denylist to remove

mutations.name: G10_the_prefix_test_is_a_bare_string_prefix
mutations.rationale: a sibling directory whose name merely starts with a governed prefix is swallowed, so an ordinary Stage-10 rule writing next door is refused and the guard becomes a dependency of the ungoverned pipeline

mutations.name: G11_the_governed_scope_is_a_boolean_rather_than_a_depth
mutations.rationale: an inner scope closing revokes the outer one, so a governed tool that calls a helper opening its own scope loses permission halfway through writing its own artifact

mutations.name: G12_the_scope_is_not_restored_when_the_body_raises
mutations.rationale: a tool that fails partway leaves the process permanently able to write governed artifacts, so the next ungoverned writer in that process is indistinguishable from a governed one

mutations.name: G14_the_verifier_borrows_the_workers_capability
mutations.rationale: may-do-the-work and may-check-the-work become one authority, so a component tricked into either holds both; the ledger refuses a grant used by anybody but its subject, which is how this was found the first time
